mainTopic: Washing hands before davening, and saying קריאת שמע loud enough to hear oneself
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבי יוחנן's teaching: relieving oneself, washing hands, putting on תפילין, saying קריאת שמע and davening together make up complete acceptance of מלכות שמים. Doing this is counted as if one built a מזבח and brought a קרבן, and רבא adds that it is even like immersing the whole body. A scholar from ארץ ישראל rules that someone without water may clean his hands with earth, a stone or a wood chip, and רבא agrees, because the פסוק says 'in cleanliness,' not 'in water.' The גמרא then limits this. For קריאת שמע one does not chase after water, but for תפילה one must search up to a פרסה ahead, or less than a מיל back. Next comes a new משנה about saying שמע: whether you must hear yourself, whether the letters must be precise, saying it in order, and fixing a mistake. The גמרא explains רבי יוסי's source from the word שמע, and then tries to match משניות and ברייתות about a deaf person separating תרומה and about saying ברכת המזון silently to the views of רבי יוסי, רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר. Finally it quotes the מגילה משנה that disqualifies a חרש, and רב מתנה says it follows רבי יוסי. The גמרא challenges this at the end of the amud, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The full order that makes up complete acceptance of Heaven's kingship
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי יוחנן's teaching: relieve oneself, wash hands, put on תפילין, say קריאת שמע, daven. That is complete מלכות שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should relieve himself, wash his hands, put on תפילין, recite קריאת שמע, and pray. This is accepting the complete kingship of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a teaching that began on the previous page. It lists the steps a person takes to accept עול מלכות שמים in a complete way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that קריאת שמע alone is not 'complete.' Adding bodily cleanliness, תפילין and תפילה around it makes the acceptance full.

keyTerms.meaning: He should relieve himself (go to the bathroom)
תפילין, the leather boxes with parchment worn on the head and arm
Complete kingship of Heaven: fully accepting הקב״ה as King

phrases.english: He should relieve himself, and wash his hands,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page: 'One who wants to accept the complete kingship of Heaven…'

phrases.english: and put on tefillin, and recite Shema,
and pray,
and this is the complete Kingdom of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's statement from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relieving oneself, washing, תפילין, קריאת שמע and תפילה together make up complete acceptance of מלכות שמים.

steps.title: Doing this order is like building an altar and bringing a sacrifice
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that whoever follows this order gets credit as if he built a מזבח and offered a קרבן, from the פסוק 'I will wash my hands in cleanliness and circle Your altar.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Anyone who relieves himself, washes his hands, puts on תפילין, recites קריאת שמע and prays is counted by the פסוק as if he built a מזבח and offered a קרבן on it. As it says: 'I will wash my hands in cleanliness, and I will circle Your altar, ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching of רבי יוחנן about the same order of actions. This one explains how great the reward is, and brings a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts washing hands right next to going around the מזבח. So washing and then davening is treated like serving at the מזבח. Davening takes the place of a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק credits him / counts it for him

steps.whyThisMatters: The word בנקיון in this פסוק becomes the key to the next two steps: what counts as washing, and whether water is required.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Anyone who relieves himself, and washes his hands,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַנִּיחַ תְּפִילִּין, וְקוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, וּמִתְפַּלֵּל —
phrases.english: and puts on tefillin, and recites Shema, and prays —
the verse credits him
as if he built an altar
and offered a sacrifice upon it,
as it is written: "I will wash my hands in cleanliness
phrases.notes: תהלים 26:6

phrases.english: and I will circle Your altar, O Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the reward for the same order of actions listed in step 1, with a פסוק as the source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following this order is counted as if one built a מזבח and offered a קרבן.

steps.title: רבא adds: it is even like immersing in a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the פסוק also shows that washing hands this way is like immersing the whole body, since it says 'I will wash' (myself) and not 'I will wash my hands.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Don't you hold that it is as if he immersed his whole body? The פסוק says 'I will wash' in cleanliness, and it does not say 'I will cause my hands to be washed.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a further point to רבי יוחנן's teaching from the same פסוק. He uses the form of a question, but he is really adding an extra layer, not attacking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ארחץ means 'I will wash' myself, which sounds like washing the whole body. If the פסוק meant only the hands, it could have said ארחיץ כפי. So washing hands before davening is counted like a full טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't the master hold…? (a question that really adds a point)
I will cause to wash (something else, like the hands)

steps.confusionAlert: Even though רבא asks 'don't you hold…', he is not disagreeing with רבי יוחנן. He agrees and adds that the credit is even bigger.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר כְּאִילּוּ טָבַל,
phrases.english: Does the Master not hold that it is as if he immersed,
as it is written: "I will wash [in cleanliness]" —
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; it finishes the words of the פסוק.

phrases.english: and it does not write "I will wash [my hands]"?
phrases.notes: ארחיץ would mean 'I will make something else wash,' just the hands. ארחץ sounds like washing all of yourself.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר כְּאִילּוּ טָבַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רבי יוחנן's reading of the same פסוק by focusing on the word ארחץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing before davening is counted as if one immersed the whole body.

steps.title: רבינא reports a surprising ruling about having no water
steps.stepSummary: רבינא tells רבא about a young scholar from ארץ ישראל who said that someone without water may wipe his hands with earth, a stone or a wood chip.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: Look at this young תלמיד חכם who came from ארץ ישראל and said: Someone who has no water to wash his hands may wipe his hands with earth, a pebble, or a wood chip.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a surprising ruling to רבא and wants to hear his reaction. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was washing hands with water. This ruling says that when there is no water, simply cleaning the hands with something else is enough. רבינא seems to find it strange and wants רבא to judge it.

keyTerms.meaning: A chip or sliver of wood

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava:
Let the Master see this young Torah scholar
who came from the West and said:
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, since it is west of בבל.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַיִם לִרְחוֹץ יָדָיו —
phrases.english: One who has no water to wash his hands —
wipes his hands with earth, and with a pebble, and with a wood chip.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reward for washing to the practical question of what to do with no water.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the ruling that one may clean his hands with earth, stone or wood instead of water correct?

steps.title: רבא approves: anything that cleans is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the scholar is right, because the פסוק says 'in cleanliness,' not 'in water.' He supports this with רב חסדא, who cursed someone who chases after water at prayer time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He spoke well. Does the פסוק say 'I will wash in water'? It says 'in cleanliness,' meaning anything that cleans. For רב חסדא used to curse someone who goes searching for water at the time of prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רבינא and backs the scholar's ruling. He proves it from the exact wording of the same פסוק and adds support from רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בנקיון shows the goal is clean hands, not water itself, so earth or a stone works. רב חסדא's curse shows that hunting for water and delaying davening is actually wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: He spoke well / he is right

steps.whatToRemember: Washing before davening is very great: like a קרבן, and even like טבילה. But the key word is בנקיון, cleanliness. If there is no water, cleaning the hands with earth, a stone or wood is enough, and one should not delay davening to chase after water.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה: when water is not available at davening time, one cleans the hands with whatever is available rather than pushing off תפילה.

phrases.english: He said to him: He spoke well,
is it written "I will wash in water"?
"In cleanliness" is written —
anything that cleans,
for indeed Rav Ḥisda would curse
one who goes searching for water
at the time of prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's report from step 4, using the פסוק from step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling is correct: the פסוק requires cleanliness, not water, so anything that cleans is enough.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word בנקיון in תהלים 26:6, and רב חסדא's curse on one who searches for water at prayer time.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Without water, one may clean his hands with any cleaning material before davening rather than delaying תפילה.

steps.title: The curse applies only to קריאת שמע, not to תפלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רב חסדא's curse to קריאת שמע. For תפלה, one must go look for water.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rule (not chasing water) is only for קריאת שמע. But for תפלה, a person must go searching for water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the rule from the last step. You should not run after water only when the issue is קריאת שמע; for תפלה you do have to look for water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא cursed someone who chases water at prayer time. The גמרא now says this applies only to קריאת שמע. The point is that קריאת שמע has a limited time, and looking for water could make you miss it. תפלה can be said through a longer part of the day, so you have time to find water.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only to; introduces a limit on a rule

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is taking back the permission to wipe hands with earth or a stone. It is only saying that for תפלה you must first make an effort to find water.

phrases.english: And these words apply to the reading of שמע,
phrases.notes: "These words" means רב חסדא's curse from the last step, against running after water.

phrases.english: but for prayer, he goes searching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב חסדא's statement from step 5 to קריאת שמע only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not chasing water applies to קריאת שמע; for תפלה one must search for water.

steps.title: How far must one go to find water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far one must go to look for water before תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And up to how far?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know one must search for water before תפלה, the גמרא asks for the distance. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Go search" needs a limit, or a person might think he has to travel forever. The question asks for a measured distance.

keyTerms.meaning: And up to how much (how far)?

phrases.english: And up to how far?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measurement of the search required in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The distance one must travel to find water before תפלה.

steps.title: Up to a פרסה
steps.stepSummary: One must go up to a פרסה to find water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to a פרסה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the distance is a פרסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a fixed, measurable limit for the search. Past that distance, one is not required to keep looking.

keyTerms.meaning: A פרסה, a distance of about four מיל

phrases.english: Up to a parasang.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One must go up to a פרסה to find water.

steps.title: A פרסה only ahead, not backward
steps.stepSummary: The פרסה is only for the road ahead. Going backward, one does not return even a מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This (a פרסה) is only in front of him. But behind him, he does not go back even a מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit: the פרסה measurement is only for water that lies ahead on his way. He does not have to turn back even a מיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going forward is on his way anyway, so a longer distance is required. Turning back is a bigger burden, so the required distance is much smaller.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of him (ahead on his way)
A מיל, a distance of about 2,000 אמות

phrases.english: And these words apply in front of him,
but behind him,
he does not go back even a mil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the פרסה rule of step 8 to the direction ahead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פרסה ahead; behind him, not even a מיל.

steps.title: Less than a מיל, he does go back
steps.stepSummary: From the wording, we learn that he does go back for water less than a מיל away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from this we learn: it is a full מיל that he does not go back. But less than a מיל, he does go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the last step's wording and closes the topic of searching for water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "he does not return a מיל" implies that a shorter distance is different. So even going backward, he must return for water that is less than a מיל away.
steps.whatToRemember: No chasing water for קריאת שמע. For תפלה: search up to a פרסה ahead, and go back for water less than a מיל behind you.

phrases.english: And from this: it is a mil that he does not go back,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: but less than a mil, he goes back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Infers the other side of the rule from step 9's wording.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Going backward, one must return for water less than a מיל away.

steps.title: משנה: Must קריאת שמע be heard by one's own ear?
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: someone who said שמע without hearing it himself fulfilled his obligation; רבי יוסי says he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who reads שמע and did not make it heard to his own ear has fulfilled his obligation. רבי יוסי says: he has not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, about how carefully קריאת שמע must be said. The first case is a מחלוקת about saying it too quietly to hear oneself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא holds that the words count even if they were not audible. רבי יוסי holds that you must at least hear your own words to fulfill the obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: Made it heard to his own ear

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who reads שמע
and did not make it heard to his ear has fulfilled his obligation.
Rabbi Yosei says: he has not fulfilled it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע וְלֹא הִשְׁמִיעַ לְאׇזְנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה; the water topic is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: valid without hearing it; רבי יוסי: not valid.

steps.title: Not saying the letters precisely
steps.stepSummary: If one did not say the letters of שמע carefully, רבי יוסי says he fulfilled his obligation; רבי יהודה says he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he read it but was not careful with its letters, רבי יוסי says he fulfilled his obligation. רבי יהודה says he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second case, about saying the letters clearly, with a מחלוקת between רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי יוסי is the lenient one, while in the previous case he was strict. רבי יהודה requires exact pronunciation of the words.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is strict in the first case (hearing) but lenient in this one (precise letters). Don't mix up who holds what.

phrases.english: If he read and was not careful with its letters,
Rabbi Yosei says: he fulfilled it.
Rabbi Yehuda says: he did not fulfill it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: valid; רבי יהודה: not valid.

steps.title: Reading out of order does not count
steps.stepSummary: One who says שמע out of order has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who reads it backward (out of order) has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules, with no מחלוקת, that קריאת שמע must be said in its proper order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the previous cases, nobody disagrees here. All the right words, said in the wrong order, do not count.

phrases.english: One who reads out of order has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third case in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קריאת שמע said out of order is not valid.

steps.title: A mistake: go back to where you erred
steps.stepSummary: One who made a mistake while saying שמע goes back to the place of the mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he read it and made a mistake, he should go back to the place where he made the mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with what to do if you make a mistake: you do not start over, you go back to the spot of the error.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows from the need for order in the previous step. Going back to the mistake keeps everything in the right sequence without repeating the whole שמע.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's four cases: hearing oneself (מחלוקת), precise letters (מחלוקת), correct order (required), and fixing a mistake (go back to that spot).

phrases.english: If he read and made a mistake,
he should go back to the place where he erred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the order requirement of step 13 with what to do after a mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After a mistake, return to the place of the error.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of רבי יוסי's view that you must hear your own שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section begins. It asks why רבי יוסי says someone who did not hear his own שמע has not fulfilled his obligation. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה (step 11), רבי יוסי says hearing yourself is required, even after the fact. The גמרא wants to know what source makes it that strict.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה from step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי יוסי's requirement to hear one's own recitation.

steps.title: The word שמע means 'make yourself hear'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי learns from the word שמע that your ears must hear what your mouth says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written 'שמע' (hear): make your ear hear what you bring out of your mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבי יוסי reads the word שמע ('hear') literally: you must actually hear the words you are saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'hear,' not just 'say.' רבי יוסי takes that to mean saying it is not enough. Your own ears must hear the words.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it is written (in a פסוק)
Bring out of your mouth, meaning say

phrases.english: Because it is written: "Hear" —
phrases.notes: דברים 6:4

phrases.english: make your ear hear
what you bring out of your mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word שמע teaches that one must hear what he says.

steps.title: The תנא קמא's reading: any language you understand
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא uses the word שמע for a different lesson: שמע may be said in any language you understand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא holds: 'שמע' means in any language that you understand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the תנא קמא does not learn רבי יוסי's rule. He uses the word שמע to teach something else: you may say שמע in any language you understand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'hear' means 'understand.' Since the תנא קמא uses the word for the language rule, he has no source that requires you to hear yourself. So he says you fulfilled your obligation even without hearing.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: 'Hear' in this reading means 'understand,' not hearing with your ears.

phrases.english: And the first tanna holds: "Hear" —
in any language that you hear.
phrases.notes: 'Hear' here means 'understand,' so any language you know works.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side's reading of the same word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word שמע teaches that שמע may be said in any language one understands.

steps.title: רבי יוסי learns both lessons
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי learns two things from the word שמע: any language, and you must hear yourself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי: learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: what does רבי יוסי do with the language lesson? He agrees with it, and learns his own rule from the same word too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that שמע can be said in any language. The only argument is whether the one word can carry a second lesson. רבי יוסי says it can, so he also requires hearing yourself.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees שמע may be said in any language you understand. רבי יוסי learns from the same word that you must also hear yourself. The תנא קמא does not.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei:
learn two things from it.
phrases.notes: He learns both lessons from the one word שמע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי יוסי deals with the תנא קמא's reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי learns both the language rule and the hearing rule from the word שמע.

steps.title: A deaf person who speaks separating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a חרש who can speak but cannot hear should not separate תרומה, but if he did, it counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: A deaf person who speaks but does not hear should not separate תרומה. And if he did separate, his תרומה is תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a different משנה about someone who cannot hear himself speak. It is setting up a question about which opinion this משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule has two levels. From the start (לכתחילה) he should not do it. After the fact (דיעבד) it is valid. This matches the question of whether hearing yourself is required.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: 'There' means a different משנה, one about תרומה.

phrases.aramaic: חֵרֵשׁ הַמְדַבֵּר וְאֵינוֹ שׁוֹמֵעַ — לֹא יִתְרוֹם.
phrases.english: A deaf person who speaks but does not hear should not separate teruma.
And if he did separate, his teruma is teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related משנה about not hearing one's own speech.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A deaf person who speaks should not separate תרומה at the start, but if he did, it is valid.

steps.title: Which תנא holds 'after the fact yes, at the start no'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא this משנה follows: valid after the fact, but not allowed at the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that a deaf person who speaks but does not hear: after the fact, yes; at the start, no?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the תרומה משנה follows. This sets up the next part, where the גמרא tries to match it to the opinions about שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא simply says one who did not hear himself fulfilled his obligation. רבי יוסי says it fails even after the fact. It is not obvious which of them holds a two-level rule of 'not at the start, but valid after the fact,' so the גמרא looks for the source.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (whose view is this)?

phrases.english: Who is the tanna
that a deaf person who speaks but does not hear
after the fact, yes,
at the start, no?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which opinion the משנה quoted in step 19 follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that not hearing is valid after the fact but not allowed at the start.

steps.title: רב חסדא: The משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the תרומה משנה follows רבי יוסי. He quotes the משנה where רבי יוסי says someone who said שמע without hearing himself did not fulfill his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי יוסי. As we learned: One who reads שמע but did not make it heard to his own ear has fulfilled his obligation. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: He has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question from step 20. He says the תרומה משנה follows רבי יוסי, and he quotes the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that hearing yourself does not hold back קריאת שמע at all. רבי יוסי requires hearing yourself. רב חסדא connects the חרש משנה, which says a חרש should not separate תרומה at the start, to רבי יוסי's view that hearing yourself matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Made it heard to his own ear

steps.confusionAlert: This looks surprising, because רבי יוסי says 'not valid' even after the fact, while the תרומה משנה says 'valid after the fact.' The next step explains how both can fit together.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: It is Rabbi Yosei,
as we learned: One who reads Shema
and did not make it heard to his ear has fulfilled his obligation,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says: He has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תרומה משנה follows רבי יוסי, who requires hearing yourself.

steps.title: Why רבי יוסי can say 'valid after the fact' for תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says 'not valid' only for קריאת שמע, which is from the Torah. With תרומה, hearing matters only for the ברכה, which is דרבנן, and the separation does not depend on the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי only said 'he has not fulfilled his obligation' about קריאת שמע, which is from the Torah. But תרומה is only a problem because of the ברכה. The ברכה is דרבנן, and the matter does not depend on the ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains how the תרומה משנה can follow רבי יוסי even though it says 'valid after the fact.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a Torah מצוה like שמע, רבי יוסי says not hearing yourself ruins the מצוה even after the fact. With תרומה, the only problem is that the חרש cannot hear his own ברכה. That ברכה is דרבנן, and the תרומה takes effect even without it, so it is valid after the fact. It is still not allowed at the start, because he would not be saying the ברכה properly.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said this in this case

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: a missing ברכה that is דרבנן does not cancel the מצוה act itself.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לֹא יָצָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei only said 'he has not fulfilled his obligation'
regarding the reading of Shema, which is from the Torah,
but terumah — the problem is because of the blessing,
phrases.notes: He means the problem is that the חרש cannot hear the ברכה he says when separating.

phrases.english: and the blessing is Rabbinic,
and the matter does not depend on the blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לֹא יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem left open by step 21: רבי יוסי says 'not valid' even after the fact, but the תרומה משנה says 'valid after the fact'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between cases (Torah מצוה versus Rabbinic ברכה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי invalidates anything done without hearing yourself, even after the fact
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a Torah מצוה like שמע is ruined. With תרומה, only the Rabbinic ברכה is affected, so it is valid after the fact.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the משנה follows רבי יוסי. Maybe רבי יהודה also says for שמע: valid after the fact, but not at the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know it is רבי יוסי? Maybe it is רבי יהודה, and he says about קריאת שמע too: after the fact, yes; at the start, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. It suggests that רבי יהודה might fit the תרומה משנה exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרומה משנה says 'not at the start, but valid after the fact.' If רבי יהודה holds the same pattern for שמע, then the משנה matches him directly, with no need for רב חסדא's Torah-versus-Rabbinic distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know
At the start, from the outset

phrases.english: And from where do we know it is Rabbi Yosei?
Perhaps it is Rabbi Yehuda?
And he says regarding the reading of Shema as well:
after the fact — yes; at the start — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא, דִּילְמָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's claim that the משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה holds 'valid after the fact, but not at the start' for שמע, then he matches the תרומה משנה exactly. In that case nothing forces us to say it follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Support from the word הקורא
steps.stepSummary: The challenger brings support: the משנה says 'one who reads,' which describes something already done. That suggests רבי יהודה allows it only after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know this, because the משנה teaches 'one who reads.' After the fact, yes; at the start, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge by looking at the exact wording of the משנה about שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not say 'a person may read without hearing himself.' It said 'one who read,' which sounds like after the fact. So it looks like even רבי יהודה only allows it after the fact.

phrases.english: Know this, since it teaches: 'One who reads,'
phrases.notes: The wording describes someone who already read, not permission to read that way.

phrases.english: after the fact — yes; at the start — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge of step 23
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה allows not hearing yourself only after the fact
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording הקורא in the משנה

steps.title: הקורא shows how far רבי יוסי goes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the support. The משנה uses הקורא to show that רבי יוסי invalidates it even after the fact. רבי יהודה allows it even at the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: The fact that it teaches 'one who reads' is to tell you how strong רבי יוסי's view is, since he says it is not valid even after the fact. For according to רבי יהודה, even at the start he fulfills his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof from הקורא and explains why the משנה used that word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The after-the-fact wording is there because of רבי יוסי. It teaches that he says 'not valid' even after it was already done. רבי יהודה actually allows it even at the start, so he does not match the תרומה משנה, and רב חסדא's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To tell you the strength (how far a view goes)

steps.whatToRemember: For now: רבי יוסי says not hearing yourself during שמע is not valid, even after the fact. רבי יהודה says it is fine even at the start. The תרומה משנה ('not at the start, but valid after the fact') follows רבי יוסי, because the hearing problem there only affects the Rabbinic ברכה. The next step challenges this.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read הקורא as proof that רבי יהודה is strict at the start. The wording is chosen to show רבי יוסי's strictness, not to limit רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: They say: This that it teaches 'one who reads'
is to tell you the strength of Rabbi Yosei's view,
who says that even after the fact it is not valid.
For if it were Rabbi Yehuda alone,
even at the start he fulfills his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הַאי דְּקָתָנֵי ״הַקּוֹרֵא״, לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ דְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 24 and defends רב חסדא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from הקורא and with it the challenge of step 23
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The after-the-fact wording is there to show רבי יוסי's strictness, not to limit רבי יהודה, who allows it even at the start

steps.title: A ברייתא about saying ברכת המזון silently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading that put the תרומה משנה with רבי יוסי. It brings a ברייתא: one should not say ברכת המזון in his heart, but if he did, he is יוצא. Whose opinion is that?
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain it? As רבי יוסי? But what about the ברייתא: A person should not say ברכת המזון in his heart, and if he did, he fulfilled his obligation. Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the explanation from the last few steps by bringing a new ברייתא about ברכת המזון. It ends by asking whose opinion this ברייתא follows, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has two parts: do not do it at the start, but after the fact it counts. Like קריאת שמע, ברכת המזון is a מצוה from the Torah, so the רבי יוסי and רבי יהודה argument applies to it. The גמרא wants to know which of them could hold this two-part ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you set up (explain) it? A phrase that questions an earlier explanation
The blessing said after eating a meal
In his heart, meaning so quietly that he does not hear himself
Who is it? Whose opinion is this?

phrases.english: How did you explain it? According to Rabbi Yosei?
phrases.notes: "It" is the תרומה משנה, which רב חסדא said follows רבי יוסי back in step 21.

phrases.english: But what about that which was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְבָרֵךְ אָדָם בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן בְּלִבּוֹ,
phrases.english: A person should not say Grace after Meals in his heart,
and if he did say it that way, he has fulfilled his obligation.
Whose opinion is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי אוֹקִימְתָּא — כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי? וְאֶלָּא הָא דְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation that ended in step 25, where רבי יהודה allows quiet recital even at the start
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the תרומה משנה follows רבי יוסי while רבי יהודה allows quiet recital even at the start
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא has a 'not at the start, but valid after the fact' ruling for a Torah מצוה. Under the current explanation, no תנא seems to hold that.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits neither רבי יוסי nor רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the problem. As explained so far, רבי יהודה allows quiet recital even at the start, and רבי יוסי does not allow it even after the fact. Neither one matches the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is neither רבי יוסי nor רבי יהודה. If it is רבי יהודה, he said it counts even at the start. If it is רבי יוסי, it does not count even after the fact!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question 'whose opinion?' by showing that, as things were explained, nobody holds this ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'not at the start, but valid after the fact.' רבי יהודה, as explained in step 25, is more lenient: valid even at the start. רבי יוסי is stricter: never valid. So the ברייתא is left without an owner, which is a sign the earlier explanation is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: After the fact, once it was already done

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: It is neither Rabbi Yosei nor Rabbi Yehuda.
For if it is Rabbi Yehuda —
didn't he say that even from the start one fulfills the obligation?
phrases.notes: This is how step 25 explained רבי יהודה's view.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yosei,
even after the fact, it does not count!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge from step 26 by showing the ברייתא has no owner
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 25 reading of רבי יהודה (valid even at the start)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יהודה allows it even at the start and רבי יוסי never allows it, then a 'not at the start, but valid after' ruling matches neither of them.

steps.title: Going back: רבי יהודה allows it only after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is forced to say the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who holds that quiet recital counts after the fact but should not be done at the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must we say? It is רבי יהודה, and after the fact, yes, it counts. From the start, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the explanation from step 25 and goes back to the earlier reading of רבי יהודה (step 24): valid only after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the ברכת המזון ברייתא fits רבי יהודה exactly: not at the start, but valid after the fact. This undoes the step 25 picture of רבי יהודה as allowing it even at the start, and the next step tests this new reading against another ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what? Used when the גמרא is forced to accept a different explanation

steps.whatToRemember: At this point: רבי יוסי says quiet recital of a Torah מצוה never counts, and רבי יהודה says it counts after the fact but should not be done at the start. Step 29 challenges this reading right away.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up: this step brings back the reading from step 24, the one step 25 had pushed away. Now רבי יהודה is 'after the fact only,' not 'even at the start.'

phrases.english: Rather, what must we say? It is Rabbi Yehuda.
And after the fact, yes; from the start, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the step 27 problem by bringing back the step 24 reading of רבי יהודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה allows quiet recital even at the start (step 25).
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה allows quiet recital only after the fact, so the ברכת המזון ברייתא follows him.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: a deaf person may separate תרומה from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא taught by רבי יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי: a deaf person who speaks but cannot hear may separate תרומה even at the start. Whose opinion can that be?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the ברייתא that רבי יהודה son of רבי שמעון בן פזי taught: A deaf person who speaks but does not hear may separate תרומה from the start. Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that רבי יהודה says 'only after the fact,' the גמרא brings a ברייתא that allows a deaf person to separate תרומה even at the start. It asks whose opinion this is, setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deaf person cannot hear his own ברכה. If רבי יהודה allows this only after the fact and רבי יוסי allows it even less, who allows it at the start? The new reading from step 28 seems to leave this ברייתא without an owner.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf person (here, one who can speak but cannot hear)

phrases.english: But what about that which was taught by

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi:
phrases.notes: This is a different רבי יהודה, not the תנא who argues with רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: A deaf person who speaks but does not hear —
may separate תרומה even from the start,
whose opinion is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְתָנֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the step 28 reading of רבי יהודה (after the fact only)
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that רבי יהודה allows not hearing oneself only after the fact
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lets a deaf person separate תרומה even at the start. With רבי יהודה now 'after the fact only' and רבי יוסי stricter, neither seems to match it.

steps.title: The deaf-person ברייתא fits neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that lets a deaf person separate תרומה even at the start matches neither רבי יהודה (only after the fact) nor רבי יוסי (not even after the fact).
steps.simpleTranslation: It is neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי. If it is רבי יהודה, he said: after the fact, yes; at the start, no. If it is רבי יוסי, he said: not even after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the problem with the ברייתא it just quoted. Neither opinion allows a deaf person to separate תרומה at the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to step 28, רבי יהודה allows quiet recital only בדיעבד, and רבי יוסי invalidates it even בדיעבד. The ברייתא allows it לכתחלה, which is more lenient than both. So nobody seems to hold this way.

keyTerms.meaning: After the fact, once it was already done
At the start, as the proper way to act
But he said! (pointing to a known opinion)

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: It is neither Rabbi Yehuda nor Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא about the deaf person separating תרומה from step 29.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yehuda —
didn't he say: after the fact, yes,
at the start, no?
If it is Rabbi Yosei —
didn't he say: even after the fact, no?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the question opened in step 29 by showing why the ברייתא fits no one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way the opinions of רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי were set up in step 28.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows לכתחלה. רבי יהודה allows only דיעבד, and רבי יוסי allows not even דיעבד. So no one fits.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's own view versus his teacher's view
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is רבי יהודה, who allows it even at the start. The ברכת המזון ברייתא (only after the fact) is his teacher's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it really is רבי יהודה, and he allows it even at the start. It is not a problem: this ברייתא is his own view, and that one is his teacher's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both ברייתות come from רבי יהודה's circle. One gives his own opinion, and the other gives the opinion of his teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא goes back to saying רבי יהודה allows quiet speech even לכתחלה, so the תרומה ברייתא is his. The ברכת המזון ברייתא, which allows it only בדיעבד, follows the view of his teacher. That is why the two seem to clash. The next step shows that רבי יהודה does quote this stricter view from his teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (going back to an earlier idea)
And it is not a problem

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ברייתות. The תרומה ברייתא (allowed even at the start) is רבי יהודה's OWN view. The ברכת המזון ברייתא (only after the fact) is his TEACHER's view.

phrases.english: Rather, it really is Rabbi Yehuda,
and he allows it even at the start.
phrases.notes: The deaf person may separate תרומה even at the start, just like the ברייתא says.

phrases.english: And it is not a problem:
this one is his own view, that one is his teacher's.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the תרומה ברייתא. "That one" is the ברכת המזון ברייתא from step 26.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem from step 30 by assigning the two ברייתות to two different people.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources: one is the תנא's own view, the other is his teacher's view that he reports.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יהודה allows quiet recital only בדיעבד, so the תרומה ברייתא fit nobody.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה himself allows it even לכתחלה. The ברכת המזון ברייתא reflects his teacher, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: Proof that רבי יהודה reports his teacher's view on קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: A source shows רבי יהודה quoting רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: one must say שמע loud enough to hear. רבי מאיר argues that what counts is the heart's intention.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: One who reads שמע must make it heard to his own ears, as it says, "Hear, Israel, ה׳ is our God, ה׳ is One." רבי מאיר said to him: It says, "which I command you today, upon your heart." The words follow the intention of the heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof that רבי יהודה has a teacher, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, whose view he reports about saying שמע out loud. The same source also brings רבי מאיר's lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns from the word "שמע" (hear) that one should make his words heard, which matches the stricter ברכת המזון ברייתא. רבי מאיר learns from "על לבבך" that the heart's intention is what matters, so saying it out loud is not needed even at the start. רבי מאיר's view becomes important in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: That he makes it heard to his own ears

phrases.english: As we learned:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is the teacher (רבו) mentioned in step 31.

phrases.english: One who reads Shema
must make it heard to his own ears,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ ה׳ אֶחָד״.
phrases.english: as it says: "Hear, Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One."
phrases.notes: דברים 6:4

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said to him:
Look, it says:
"which I command you today, upon your heart" —
phrases.notes: דברים 6:6

phrases.english: after the intention of the heart
are the words.
phrases.notes: Literally "they, they are the words." He means the words count based on what the heart intends.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up step 31 by showing that רבי יהודה does report a stricter view from his teacher.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי יהודה reports his teacher's stricter view, separate from his own.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of רבי יהודה in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה about making קריאת שמע audible, together with רבי מאיר's reply.

steps.title: Second answer: the תרומה ברייתא follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: Now that רבי מאיר's view has been quoted, רבי יהודה can agree with his teacher. The תרומה ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, and the ברכת המזון ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, you can even say that רבי יהודה agrees with his teacher. It is not a problem: this one is רבי מאיר, that one is רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer, using רבי מאיר's view from the source it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to say that רבי יהודה disagrees with his teacher. He can hold only בדיעבד, like the ברכת המזון ברייתא. The תרומה ברייתא, which allows it לכתחלה, fits רבי מאיר, who says the heart's intention is what matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this point

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers for the deaf person separating תרומה at the start: (1) it is רבי יהודה's own view, while his teacher holds only בדיעבד; or (2) רבי יהודה agrees with his teacher, and the lenient ברייתא is רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
phrases.notes: Now that the full source has been quoted, including רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.english: you can even say
Rabbi Yehuda holds like his teacher.
And it is not a problem:

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: this one is Rabbi Meir, that one is Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: The תרומה ברייתא is רבי מאיר. The ברכת המזון ברייתא is רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי מאיר from step 32 to give a second answer to step 30, different from step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving the lenient ברייתא to a different תנא, רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Step 31 needed רבי יהודה to disagree with his teacher in order to explain the lenient ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה can agree with his teacher (only בדיעבד). The lenient תרומה ברייתא is רבי מאיר's view.

steps.title: משנה about who may read the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in מסכת מגילה: everyone may read the מגילה except a חרש, a שוטה and a קטן. רבי יהודה allows a קטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: Everyone is fit to read the מגילה, except a deaf person, a person without sound mind, and a minor. And רבי יהודה allows a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה from another מסכת about reading the מגילה. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists a deaf person among those who may not read the מגילה. That ties back to the question of reading without hearing yourself. רבי יהודה disagrees only about a minor, and the גמרא will now ask who the unnamed opinion is.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there (in a משנה in another place)
A deaf person, a person without sound mind, and a minor

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: "There" means מסכת מגילה.

phrases.english: Everyone is fit to read the Megilla,
except a deaf person, a person without sound mind, and a minor.
And Rabbi Yehuda allows a minor.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִים לִקְרוֹת אֶת הַמְּגִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a parallel discussion about the מגילה, which also involves a deaf person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone may read the מגילה except a חרש, a שוטה and a קטן. רבי יהודה allows a קטן.

steps.title: Who holds a deaf person's reading fails even after the fact?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is behind the מגילה משנה that disqualifies a חרש even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that a deaf person's reading does not count, even after the fact?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks back at the משנה in מסכת מגילה from the last step and asks whose opinion it follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That משנה lists who is כשר to read the מגילה and leaves out the חרש. That suggests his reading does not count even if he already read. The גמרא wants to know which תנא holds that strict view.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (who taught this)?
After the fact (he already did it)

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who taught
that a deaf person is not valid even after the fact?
phrases.notes: This points back to the מגילה משנה, which leaves the deaf person off the list of people who are כשר to read.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תָּנָא חֵרֵשׁ דִּיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the מגילה משנה quoted in step 34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a חרש's reading is not valid even after the fact.

steps.title: רב מתנה: it is רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה says the מגילה משנה follows רבי יוסי. In our משנה, רבי יוסי holds that one who did not hear his own שמע has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: It is רבי יוסי. As we learned: One who reads שמע but did not make it heard to his own ear has fulfilled his obligation. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: He has not fulfilled it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה answers that the מגילה משנה follows רבי יוסי. He supports this from our משנה about קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that if you did not hear your own words, you have not fulfilled your obligation, even after the fact. A חרש cannot hear himself at all. So by רבי יוסי his reading never counts, which fits the מגילה משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Made it heard to his own ear

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא.
phrases.english: Rav Mattana said: It is Rabbi Yosei.
As we learned: One who reads Shema
and did not make it heard to his own ear has fulfilled his obligation,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says: He has not fulfilled it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מגילה משנה follows רבי יוסי, who holds that not hearing your own words fails even after the fact.
steps.confusionAlert: In our משנה רבי יהודה is the lenient one (יצא) and רבי יוסי is the strict one (לא יצא). Don't flip them.

steps.title: How do we know it is רבי יוסי and not even after the fact?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב מתנה: how do we know the מגילה משנה is רבי יוסי, and that it means even after the fact?
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know that it is רבי יוסי, and that even after the fact it is not valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב מתנה's answer. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will suggest another way to read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מתנה assumed the מגילה משנה means a חרש is not valid even after the fact. The גמרא asks what forces that reading. Maybe the משנה only means he should not read in the first place, and it follows רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: From where do you know that it is Rabbi Yosei
and that even after the fact it is not valid?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא וְדִיעֲבַד נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind רב מתנה's answer in step 36.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מתנה's claim that the מגילה משנה follows רבי יוסי and means 'not even after the fact'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the מגילה משנה forces the 'even after the fact' reading. It could mean he should not read in the first place, which could fit רבי יהודה.
